newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-DEL PIERO SAYS PROBLEMS ARE IN THE PAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEL PIERO SAYS PROBLEMS ARE IN THE PAST.

text.p: Striker Alessandro Del Piero, scorer of the goal that earned Juventus the World Club Cup on Tuesday, declared his early season fitness problems over and promised fans more triumphs ahead.
"I went through a weak patch (at the start of the season) but I never felt marginalised," he told a news conference after the 1-0 win over Argentina's River Plate in Tokyo.

"The coaching staff and my team mates did everything possible to help me recover. In the last few weeks, with the goals in Manchester and in Tokyo, I have definitely overcome my problems. I am very happy."
Del Piero also scored the goal that gave Juventus a 1-0 victory against Manchester United in the Champions' League last week and secured their place in the quarter-finals.
"In the same year Juventus have now won the European Cup and the Intercontinental Cup. And I can assure our fans that we are not going to let it rest there," the 22-year-old said.

Coach Marcello Lippi thanked former Juventus players who helped the club reach the final -- including Gianluca Vialli and Fabrizio Ravanelli now in England and Portugal's Paolo Sousa playing in the German Bundesliga.
He also praised Alen Boksic, who missed two good chances but was influential as ever.

"The Croat is a great player," said Lippi. "He's very fast, strong and is never tired even when his team mates are beginning to fade physically. Boksic carries on attacking, wounding opponents' defences. I applaud him."
